D4_4a N03: Seasonal-Temperature CAPEX Trap Under Fixed Membrane Permeability

An SWRO train has feed 0.360 m³/s, TDS 36.5 g/L, TSS 0.03 g/L, P1=69 bar(a), ηP1=ηP2=0.82 and PX efficiency 0.95, with year-round product ≥12,900 m³/d. An engineer proposes sizing 16,000 m² using only the 15°C case. Use simulate_swro_system to check 15/25/32°C and test 17,000 and 18,000 m² at 32°C. The model holds A_comp=4.2×10⁻¹² constant with temperature. Determine the year-round area on the specified discrete grid, the CAPEX increment, and explain why the temperature trend must not be generalized as a universal membrane rule.

Final conclusion

Checking only 15°C would falsely accept 16,000 m² because product is 12,954.88 m³/d; the fixed-A_comp model gives only 12,396.04 m³/d at 32°C. At 32°C, 17,000 m² still produces only 12,867.00 m³/d, while 18,000 m² reaches 13,312.24 m³/d. The specified discrete year-round design is therefore 18,000 m² at CAPEX USD 26.286 million (2018), about USD 0.309 million above the apparent 15°C/16,000 m² design. This counterintuitive trend reflects fixed membrane-permeability assumptions and must be rechecked with vendor temperature-correction factors for procurement.
